title: Throughput Steward: Elasticity Panel + Compact Change Chronicle
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a new Console surface called 'Throughput Steward' that unifies scaling controls, guaranteed throughput configuration, and a compact immutable change chronicle. The goal is to give operators one place to tune per-fleet elasticity, set throughput SLAs, preview expected cost impact, and review a concise history of configuration changes with rollback pointers. This is targeted at Dedicated customers and Platform teams who operate multiple fleets and need fast, audit-friendly controls without exposing low-level infra knobs.
acceptance_criteria: Elasticity Panel exposes: target throughput slider (rps), burst buffer setting, and three autoscale templates (Conservative, Balanced, Aggressive)
Users can define a guaranteed throughput value (hard SLO) that triggers capacity reservations and a separate best-effort throttle value
Cost estimator displays delta in estimated monthly GPU-hours and token-unit cost for changes before save
Compact Change Chronicle shows timestamp, author, summary, diff link, and a single-click 'Revert to this config' action (backend returns a reversible config ID)
Panel integrates with existing rollouts system for canary/cutover and honors fleet-level RBAC and approval flows
Telemetry events emitted for every apply/preview and surfaced in Console telemetry view (route, model, fleet tags)
tasks: Design mocks for Elasticity Panel and Chronicle (DES-3140) - handoff to engineering by 2026-02-20
API: extend fleet-config API to accept guaranteed_throughput and reserve_capacity flags (ENG-9784)
Backend: implement reversible config snapshot IDs and rollback endpoint (ENG-9812)
Cost estimation service hook and UI delta (ENG-9860)
Telemetry: add preview/apply event types + attributes (ENG-9899)
QA: stress test autoscale templates under synthetic traffic profiles and validate SLO enforcement
Beta rollout: select two existing Dedicated customers and 3 internal fleets for early feedback
decisions: Expose three curated autoscale templates rather than full policy DSL to reduce cognitive load for operators
Enable YAML editor via 'Advanced' toggle for power users, but hide by default to avoid misconfigurations
Implement optimistic preview-first UX: compute cost and impact without immediate apply; require explicit confirmation to commit
Chronicle will store immutable snapshots (config IDs) instead of diffs to simplify rollback semantics
tradeoffs: Simplicity vs Flexibility: limiting templates reduces mistakes but may not fit all edge workloads
Immediate reservation of capacity for guaranteed throughput increases cost predictability but reduces burst efficiency
Surface-level cost estimates will be conservative; precise billing reconciliation remains offline and can differ
Storing full immutable snapshots increases metadata storage but simplifies audit and revert operations
